question.text: A 'Pure Offshore' fund making direct investments into Indian investee companies must typically register with SEBI under which regulation?

explanation.text: The Logic: A Pure Offshore fund is not an AIF. It invests into India directly and must register as a Foreign Venture Capital Investor (FVCI) under SEBI (FVCI) Regulations or as a Foreign Portfolio Investor (FPI) under SEBI (FPI) Regulations - depending on the asset class and strategy. The Trap: AIF Regulations apply only to Indian onshore AIFs. MF Regulations are for mutual funds. Merchant Banker is a licensing statute, not an investor registration. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C comparative table tests this directly. XIX-A distributor angle asks which products they can sell. Manager's Pro-Tip: FVCI status gives exemption from IPO lock-in and Takeover Code - a strategic advantage for pre-IPO Cat I strategies. Structure offshore feeders as FVCIs where possible.
